Hi Sarah — thanks again for the call earlier today. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we can align on the right deployment mode for NovaMed's migration: 

1) Summary from our discovery:
- Current setup: Evaluation workloads running via another LLM API (rate-limited by token quotas) plus an internal self-hosted GPU cluster used for some latency-sensitive models.
- Key constraints: PHI handling requirements for certain workflows, predictable latency for clinical decision support, and a target monthly token baseline + burst for spikes.

2) Deployment options that match your needs:
- Hosted API: fastest time-to-value, no infra to manage, good for non-PHI and low-risk workloads.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pool with predictable throughput and SLA — recommended for production clinical pipelines that need isolation but still want managed operations.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking and KMS/HSM for the strictest compliance (recommended if NovaMed wants full control over network egress and audited keys).

3) Migration patterns we see and recommended approach for NovaMed:
- From another LLM API: we can ramp traffic to Redwood Hosted for non-PHI workloads while migrating sensitive flows to Dedicated or Private.
- From self-hosted GPU clusters: we typically run a short pilot on Dedicated to match throughput and then cut-over once autoscaling and KV cache behavior are validated.

Next steps I propose:
- I'll share a short migration checklist and a Dedicated sizing worksheet for your infra team to review (attached).
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Rafael and Dylan to validate network/keys and sizing (30-45m).
- If procurement is required, we can surface an initial SOW/draft contract for review.

Do these next steps work for you? If yes, I can coordinate times — Rafael and I are available Wed/Thu this week PST.

Best,

Hi Sarah — a few quick technical points ahead of tomorrow's call: 

- Dedicated + KMS: We support customer-managed KMS for Dedicated via VPC and Cloud KMS integrations; for strict HSM requirements we can discuss Private (on-prem) options or bring-your-own-HSM via our Private offering.
- Perf delta vs mixed cluster: Dedicated homogeneous A100 pool will generally reduce tail latency and improve throughput by ~15-25% versus mixed older GPUs due to consistent kernel performance and larger memory for KV cache. We'll validate with the sizing workbook you provided.
- Tokenization / prompt compatibility: Models behave the same in our runtime as upstream open checkpoints; differences with OpenAI mainly come from model family/version. We provide model mapping and small compatibility shim for stop sequences and streaming semantics that makes transition low-effort for most clients.

I attached a short checklist excerpt below and a note on expected validation tests during the pilot:
- Pilot tests: 95th pct latency, throughput at target qps, KV cache hit rate, deterministic sampling checks, and cost per 1M tokens baseline.

Happy to cover these in the call and run a short load validation run on Dedicated before any cutover.

Thanks,
Dylan Brooks
